headline: Ansar Allah (Ansar Allah) siege of Taiz may amount to the war crime of starvation
dek: [PRIMARY-SOURCE CLAIM - HRW's own finding] Human Rights Watch says the Ansar Allah (Ansar Allah) siege of Taiz (Taizz), Yemen's third-largest city, has drastically worsened since October 2026, when Ansar Allah forces fully encircled the city and blocked and attacked the remaining major supply route, causing…
sources: Human Rights Watch report 'Yemen: Ansar Allah Depriving Taizz Civilians of Food, Medicine' (Oct 29), via Al Jazeera liveblog + ReliefWeb copy
fault_line: Is the Taiz siege 'Yemen's Gaza' -- a starvation crime the world ignores -- or, as the Ansar Allah side claims, a government blockade blamed on the wrong side?

sections.what_happened: [PRIMARY-SOURCE CLAIM - HRW's own finding] Human Rights Watch says the Ansar Allah (Ansar Allah) siege of Taiz (Taizz), Yemen's third-largest city, has drastically worsened since October 2026, when Ansar Allah forces fully encircled the city and blocked and attacked the remaining major supply route, causing severe shortages of fuel, food, water, medicine, cooking gas and humanitarian access. HRW says the siege 'may amount to war crime of using starvation as a method of warfare'; it quotes researcher Niku Jafarnia: 'Renewed efforts by the Ansar Allah to cut off food, water, and medicine to Taizz show their utter disregard for civilian lives.' HRW spoke to 15 people in October (5 residents, 4 doctors, 6 civil-society workers) and cites the World Food Programme as unable to reach more than 600,000 people in Taiz dependent on assistance. This is DISTINCT from HRW's Oct 26 report on the Oct 18 Hayjat al-Abd road attack (also Taiz, road-dynamiting finding) -- today's report is the wider encirclement/starvation assessment, not a repeat of the road-attack item. Ansar Allah counterclaim on record: a Ansar Allah spokesperson told HRW on Oct 21 that Yemeni government forces, not Ansar Allah forces, were blocking roads into the city; HRW reports residents, civil-society workers and UN officials place responsibility on the Ansar Allah.
sections.what_verified: HRW is NOT in the declared-tier registry, so it never counts toward corroboration; the counted declared family is Al Jazeera (T2, STATE QA) as the liveblog carrier, plus the HRW primary document itself as the attributed originator. ReliefWeb copy is also undeclared and does not add a family.
sections.what_disputed: Ansar Allah spokesperson (Oct 21, via HRW): government forces block the roads, not Ansar Allah forces. HRW's own Oct 26 road-attack report must not be merged into this item -- different finding (road dynamiting Oct 18) from today's encirclement assessment. No independent second verification of the full-encirclement claim retrieved in-window.
sections.why_matters: HRW's starvation finding on Taiz: 600,000 cut off from aid as the siege tightens -- the Yemen war's other front, away from the airport strikes.
sections.context: Background: NEW IN-WINDOW -- Human Rights Watch: Ansar Allah (Ansar Allah) siege of Taiz may amount to the war crime of starvation; full encirclement since October 2026, 600,000+ cut off from aid

totw_analysis: Our read: HRW's starvation finding on Taiz: 600,000 cut off from aid as the siege tightens -- the Yemen war's other front, away from the airport strikes. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Is the Taiz siege 'Yemen's Gaza' -- a starvation crime the world ignores -- or, as the Ansar Allah side claims, a government blockade blamed on the wrong side?
